jupyter: python3

The codebook defines the charting form. It lists every variable charted for each included source of evidence, as PRISMA-ScR item 11 requires. The form is a draft and will be revised after piloting on a sample of sources.

The form has two tables, both CSV files in `data/raw/`. The sources table has one row per included source. The factors table has one row per factor that a source reports, so a source with five factors has five rows there. The tables are linked by `source_id`. Closed variables take only the values listed below, in lowercase. This page and [03-charting](analysis/03-charting.ipynb) both read the variables from `codebook.yml`, so a change is made there once.

## Sources

`included_sources_raw.csv`. One row per included source of evidence.

| Variable | Definition | Allowed values | Required |
|---|---|---|---|
| `source_id` | Identifier of the source of evidence. Reports of the same study share one `source_id`. | Free text | yes |
| `record_id` | Identifier of the primary report in `deduplicated_records.csv`. | Free text | yes |
| `tier` | Context tier from the [protocol](research-protocol.qmd). | `1`, `2` | yes |
| `field` | Field of research the source concerns. | `health`, `other`, `cross-disciplinary` | yes |
| `field_detail` | Specific field or subfield, such as genomics or archaeology. | Free text | no |
| `source_type` | Type of source. | `empirical`, `review`, `policy-guidance`, `opinion`, `other` | yes |
| `peer_reviewed` | Whether the source was peer reviewed. | `yes`, `no` | no |
| `data_origin` | Origin of the data the source concerns. `research` means collected for research. `routine-reused` means collected for operational or care purposes and reused for research. | `research`, `routine-reused`, `mixed`, `unclear` | no |
| `region` | Country or region of the data, institutions, or participants. | Free text | no |
| `notes` | Anything that affects interpretation. | Free text | no |

## Factors

`included_factors_raw.csv`. One row per factor that a source reports. A source that reports five factors has five rows, each with its own type, category, and level.

| Variable | Definition | Allowed values | Required |
|---|---|---|---|
| `source_id` | The source that reports the factor. It must appear in `included_sources_raw.csv`. | Free text | yes |
| `factor` | The specific factor, in the source's words or a close paraphrase. | Free text | yes |
| `factor_type` | Kind of factor. | `barrier`, `facilitator`, `governance-mechanism` | yes |
| `factor_category` | Initial categories from @vanpanhuis2014, revised during synthesis. Left empty until the factor is coded. | `technical`, `motivational`, `economic`, `political`, `legal`, `ethical`, `other` | no |
| `level` | Level at which the factor operates. `system` covers national, sectoral, and international levels. When a source reports the same factor at two levels, enter one row for each. | `individual`, `institutional`, `system` | no |
| `notes` | Anything that affects interpretation. | Free text | no |



`03-charting.ipynb` stops with an error when a charted value is not allowed, a required cell is empty, or a `source_id` or `record_id` does not match the other files.
